description_full: MINISO Group Holding Limited, an investment holding company, engages in the retail and wholesale of design-led lifestyle and pop toy products in Mainland China, the rest of Asia, North and Latin America, Europe, and internationally. The company offers products in various categories, including home decor products, small electronics, textiles, accessories, beauty tools, toys, cosmetics, personal care products, snacks, fragrances and perfumes, and stationeries and gifts under the MINISO brand; and blind boxes, toy bricks, model figures, model kits, collectible dolls, Ichiban Kuji, and other popular toys under the TOP TOY brand. It also engages in brand licensing activity; and online sale of lifestyle products. MINISO Group Holding Limited was founded in 2013 and is based in Guangzhou, China.

financial_summary: MINISO Group Holding Limited is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $3.1B market cap on $2.4B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +20% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +5.0pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 72% against a 9% cost of capital — a 64-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 35%.

The business throws off $196M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.82× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 36× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 7.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
